newsitem.title: SWEDEN: FDA gives Astra's Losec new patents.
newsitem.headline: FDA gives Astra's Losec new patents.

text.p: Swedish drug company Astra said Tuesday the U.S. Food and Drug Administration updated its approved drugs list with another three patents for Astra's blockbuster anti-ulcer drug, Losec.
Astra said the FDA had updated its Orange Book, entitled "Approved Drug Products with Therapeutic Equivalence Evaluations," to include three additional patents for Prilosec, or Losec (omeprazole).
"The FDA has included in the new listing a patent covering the active metabolite of omeprazole which was granted in 1987 and will expire in the U.S. in the year 2005," Astra said.

"This patent complements three earlier Astra patents included in the Orange Book: one substance patent expiring in the U.S. in the year 2001 and two formulation patents expiring in 2007 in the U.S.," it said.
"Additionally, the FDA has listed two patents covering omeprazole's indication for the eradication of the H. pylori bacterium, which causes 90 percent of peptic ulcers," it said.
These patents will expire in the United States in 2010 and 2014, Astra said.
Astra's American Depositary Receipts were up $2.125 at $4.375 on the New York Stock Exchange.
